notes:
- Mid-market SaaS (subscription billing) evaluating Redwood for primary billing/support agent workload.
- Main goal: conversational agent for billing/subscription support (Stripe + Zuora integration). Tool calling + structured JSON outputs required (actions: invoice_lookup, refund_issue, subscription_modify).
- Latency is the big gating factor: product/infra leadership want p95 end-to-end < 300ms for streaming responses when calling external payment APIs; p99 under load target discussed. Quote from VP Eng: "We need consistent 2xx tool calls under 300ms for interactive support flows."
- Preference: start on Hosted API for speed of integration + streaming/tool-calling features; evaluate Dedicated for predictable throughput and cost when POC shows >50k monthly conversations.
- Cost sensitivity: moderate. Will trade some model size for quantization/edge variants if latency/cost improvements are clear. Interested in Redwood Optimize recommendations for batching & quantization.
- Security: require SSO/SAML, audit logs, KMS integration for key material, DPA + EU residency for subset of customer data. SOC2 in progress; client legal needs SOC2 + DPA before signing.
- POC asks: synthetic traffic at 200 RPS with 30 concurrent agent sessions; scripted Stripe/Zuora callbacks stubbed; measure p50/p95/p99 for token streaming and tool-call round-trip. Evaluate structured output correctness (JSON schema validation) and automatic retry/fallback behavior.
- Integration notes: existing backend uses Zuora for invoicing and Stripe for card ops. They want Redwood tool-calling to run pre-authorized actions (idempotent ops) and return normalized JSON with fields: action, status, amount, currency, invoice_id, user_message, followup_required.
- Sales tact: AE to push Dedicated TCO scenarios vs Hosted at 100k+ messages/month. Include canary/fallback policy examples.
- Stakeholders: VP Eng (decision), Head of Product (UX constraints), SRE (latency SLO), Legal (DPA), Security (SOC2).
- Tone of notes: shorthand in CRM, lots of checkboxes left to close; key friction points are SOC2 + EU residency + final pricing for Dedicated.
